providers.market_view: The German equity market is currently characterized by a robust upward trend, with the benchmark DAX reaching historic highs driven by strong corporate earnings from industrial and insurance heavyweights. While technical indicators suggest a bullish momentum supported by rising moving averages, the index is approaching psychologically significant resistance levels and exhibiting some overbought signals on short-term RSI oscillators. Market sentiment is balanced between optimism over solid domestic corporate performance and external pressures from a strengthening US dollar and rising government bond yields. Investors are increasingly selective, shifting focus from broad index-linked gains to specific companies demonstrating superior operational resilience and record order backlogs.

# Germany's Merck Raises Guidance Again on Growth Across Units

By Adria Calatayud

Germany's Merck KGaA raised its annual guidance for the third time this year, citing top-line growth across its businesses and favorable currency movements.

The Darmstadt, Germany-based conglomerate said Thursday that it expects full-year net sales to range between 21.5 billion and 21.9 billion euros ($23.84 billion-$24.29 billion), against its prior forecast of between 21 billion and 21.8 billion euros.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization excluding one-time items for the year are forecast at between 6.2 billion and 6.4 billion euros, which compares with previous guidance of 5.9 billion to 6.3 billion euros.
